The story does not provide diverse perspectives; it is told entirely from the single, first-person perspective of an unnamed narrator. The other characters in the story—the man and the woman—are observed purely from a distance, never speak, and do not have their internal thoughts or viewpoints shared directly with the reader. While the narrator engages in the questionable and somewhat unsettling behavior of following strangers home and watching them through their window, their perspective is driven by quiet, aimless curiosity and melancholy rather than any repugnant or deeply objectionable beliefs, and it remains the sole viewpoint in the narrative.
